name: Minimum
description: Helps Geometry Dash run smoother on weaker hardware, mostly in particle heavy levels. It skips drawing particles that are not doing anything, can cap how many a level spawns, and adds a button to the pause menu and the level editor with a live frame time card and a few quick toggles. There is also a lower latency option, a frame rate unlock on phones and a precise frame limiter on PC. It changes how the game is drawn, never how it plays. Works on Windows, macOS, Android and iOS.

mod-enabled.name: Enable Minimum
mod-enabled.description: Master switch. Turn it off to compare the game with and without the mod, no restart needed.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: Quick profile for particles and the background frame rate. Balanced: 256 particles. Performance: 128. Extreme: 48. Super Performance: 16 particles, Low Detail Mode on and the lowest background frame rate, the plainest look and the fastest. Custom uses the settings below. Enter the level again after changing it.

adaptive-target-fps.name: Target FPS
adaptive-target-fps.description: The frame rate you want to hold, usually your screen refresh rate (60, 90, 120, 144...). The FPS counter colors, the adaptive particle cap and the Android CPU hint all use it.

pause-button-corner.name: Pause Menu Button
pause-button-corner.description: Where the Minimum logo sits in the pause menu. If another button is in the way it moves to the nearest free spot. Hidden removes it (you can still open Minimum from the Geode mod list).

toggle-mod-key.name: Hotkey: Toggle Minimum
toggle-mod-key.description: Turns Minimum on or off instantly, so you can compare with and without it.

toggle-stats-key.name: Hotkey: Toggle Stats Line
toggle-stats-key.description: Shows or hides the stats line.

low-latency.name: Low Latency Mode
low-latency.description: Makes the CPU wait for the GPU after every frame so clicks show up sooner. Works on PC, Mac, Android and iOS. How much it helps depends on the device: on a slow GPU it can cost FPS, and on a phone that is limited by its CPU it may change nothing. It only runs while the game holds its frame rate and switches itself off for a while if FPS drops. Turn on Detailed in Stats Detail to see 'sync on' when it is running. Off by default.

skip-idle-particles.name: Skip Idle Particle Draws
skip-idle-particles.description: Does not draw particle systems that have no live particles. Looks exactly the same.

cap-particles.name: Cap Particle Pool Size
cap-particles.description: Limits how many particles a single system can hold. Only affects systems created after the change, so enter the level again. Lower cap means more FPS in heavy levels and thinner effects.

particle-cap.name: Particle Cap
particle-cap.description: Max particles per system. 128 keeps normal effects intact and trims extreme particle spam. 32 is aggressive.

adaptive-cap.name: Adaptive Particle Cap
adaptive-cap.description: If the game keeps missing the Target FPS, the particle cap is lowered step by step (down to 1/8) and raised again once things are smooth. On Android the cap also drops while the phone is hot and comes back after it cools down. Visual only.

cull-offscreen-particles.name: Skip Offscreen Particles
cull-offscreen-particles.description: Does not draw particle systems that are far outside the screen. They are still updated, so effects stay in sync and look the same when they come back on screen. Visual only.

spawn-budget.name: Particle Spawn Budget
spawn-budget.description: How many particle systems per frame get a full pool during a level. 0 is off. Systems past the limit still exist, but with a pool of 4 particles, so a burst of effects looks thinner instead of stalling the frame.

low-detail.name: Low Detail Mode
low-detail.description: Turns on the game's own Low Detail Mode while Minimum is on, which skips decoration effects like speed particles and the landing ring. Your saved Options are not changed, and it goes back to what you had when you turn this off. Takes full effect on the next attempt. The Super Performance preset turns this on for you.

fps-unlock.name: Unlock Frame Rate
fps-unlock.description: Asks the system for more frames per second than the game's default 60. Your screen's refresh rate still decides the real maximum. Off by default.

fps-limit.name: Frame Rate Limit
fps-limit.description: The highest frame rate asked for when Unlock Frame Rate is on. 120 suits a 120 Hz screen. Values above your screen's refresh rate do nothing.

android-cpu-hint.name: CPU Speed Hint
android-cpu-hint.description: Tells Android how long each frame takes so it can raise the CPU speed before a heavy frame arrives, which helps with stutter. Needs Android 13 or newer, does nothing on older versions. May use a bit more battery.

timer-resolution.name: 1 ms Timer Resolution
timer-resolution.description: Asks Windows for 1 ms timer wakeups instead of ~15.6 ms. Reduces uneven frame pacing when the game waits for the next frame. Slightly higher idle power use.

disable-power-throttling.name: Disable Power Throttling
disable-power-throttling.description: Opts the game out of Windows efficiency mode (EcoQoS) so it is not moved to slow cores or low clocks. Useful on laptops and Windows 11.

process-priority.name: Process Priority
process-priority.description: Above Normal is safe. High can starve OBS or Discord. Applied immediately, no restart needed.

background-throttle.name: Throttle Drawing In Background
background-throttle.description: While the game window is not focused, draw at Background FPS. Game logic and audio keep running normally. Windows only. Turn off if you record the game with OBS window capture while it is unfocused.

background-fps.name: Background FPS
background-fps.description: Draw rate while the game window is not focused.

background-volume.name: Lower Volume When Tabbed Out
background-volume.description: Drops music and SFX when the window loses focus so other audio is clearer.

draw-divide.name: Draw Divide
draw-divide.description: OFF by default. Draws at Visual FPS while game logic keeps running at the full frame rate. Only useful if your FPS is higher than your screen refresh rate (FPS bypass / uncapped). Do not use it together with the Draw Divide mod by mat.

visual-fps.name: Visual FPS
visual-fps.description: Draw rate when Draw Divide is on. Set it to your monitor refresh rate (60, 144, 240).

precise-frame-limit.name: Precise Frame Limiter
precise-frame-limit.description: When the game's own FPS cap is off, Minimum holds each frame to your Target FPS itself, sleeping and then spinning the last millisecond for an exact pace. Uses a little more CPU. Not used while Draw Divide is on.

show-stats.name: Show FPS Counter
show-stats.description: Shows the real FPS in a corner. Green means it holds your Target FPS, yellow is close, red is bad. Shows (background) while the window is not focused and the game is being throttled.

hud-detail.name: Stats Detail
hud-detail.description: Compact shows only the FPS. Detailed adds the 1% low, frame time, logic updates per second, spikes, the Low Latency status, whether the CPU or the GPU is the bottleneck, the draw and skip counters, and CPU time on Android.

hud-corner.name: Stats Corner
hud-corner.description: Where the stats line is drawn.

spike-logger.name: Frame Spike Logger
spike-logger.description: Writes frames that take longer than the threshold to the Geode log, with the player x position and how many particle systems were created in that frame. Look for "Frame spike" in geode/logs. Off by default.

spike-threshold-ms.name: Spike Threshold (ms)
spike-threshold-ms.description: A frame longer than this counts as a spike. 40 ms is a visible stutter at 60 FPS. Lower it if you run 240 FPS and want to catch smaller hitches.

fast-alt-tab.name: Fast Alt Tab
fast-alt-tab.description: Skips the game save that happens when the window loses focus, so alt tab does not stutter. Saving on level exit and on closing the game is untouched. Not available on Android and iOS on purpose: the OS can close the app right after it goes to the background.
